Reduce his oversized bulbous thumb substantially and tuck it closely against the SIDE of the main glove, matching the small compact curved side pad in image 2. Main face-bearing red glove body must dominate silhouette; no second large round lobe beside mouth. Target thumb around one-quarter to one-third the height of main glove body, as pose permits, small and unobtrusive. Keep glove's present orientation, main body size, face placement, eye direction, cheerful expression, leather scuffs and damaged torn WHITE cuff exactly recognizable. Preserve cushion support and cuff injury. Reconstruct only tiny cushion/background area exposed by reduced thumb. Preserve ALL other characters, eye colors, hands, costumes, faces, objects, lettering, architecture, composition, lighting, framing and original aspect ratio. Do not regenerate or rearrange scene. No new glove, no limbs, no human hand inside cuff. Output complete original scene, not crop, comparison, sheet or close-up. This is correction of thumb size only.

operationsRefinements: Edit FIRST IMAGE only: correct ONLY the small red boxing glove resting on blue cushion at lower right held by short detective. His THUMB is still too tall and bulbous. Make that thumb a TINY tucked oval side pad, about HALF its current height and width, maximum one quarter the height of his large red face-bearing glove body. Primary red body and face must remain same size and orientation. Compare author-approved second reference: one dominant red glove and small discrete side thumb. Fill exposed space with blue cushion naturally. Preserve his torn white cuff, eyes, mouth, leather scuffs, pose, EVERY other character and object, all text, color, architecture and framing. Do not shrink whole glove, only thumb. No other edits. Output complete landscape scene.

Make a surgical edit to FIRST IMAGE: the little animated red boxing glove on the blue cushion held by detective at bottom right has ONE correct small round thumb on VIEWER LEFT of his face. KEEP that small left thumb exactly. There is an erroneous second red bulge on VIEWER RIGHT at lower cheek just before the white cuff. REMOVE that extra bulge and make viewer-right lower cheek a continuous smooth red glove contour meeting the existing white cuff, preserving face mouth smile and eyes. Only ONE thumb, viewer-left. Preserve ALL other image content composition text other characters unchanged. Full landscape scene output. Second image is approved anatomy reference only. No restyling.

Edit FIRST image only, localized to red boxing glove at lower right. His small single viewer-left thumb and face shape are CORRECT, preserve exactly. Restore canonical INJURY TEXTURE from SECOND image: scuffed scratched cracked red leather across face/body (without obscuring face), and ragged visibly TORN/frayed white cuff edge with a dark notch in far right cuff edge. He is still recovering, do not make him new or fully repaired. Keep same small thumb and continuous viewer-right cheek with no extra red bump. Restore only scuffs and cuff tear; no new anatomy. Every other part of full landscape scene unchanged. SECOND image for injury texture only, not thumb anatomy.
review: Each replacement has one compact side thumb, a dominant face-bearing glove body, supported torn cuff and scuffed leather. Operations intermediate with second red bulge rejected; cuff damage restored in final edit.
continuityNote: Historical review of the earlier design. For current Book Three art use the author-approved Fist character sheet, sculpted face, single swept-back thumb fold and red cuff with inset black-outlined white panel.
